papers.title: MAESTRO: Orchestrating Robotics Modules with Coding Agents for Zero-Shot Generalist Robots
papers.abstract: Today’s dominant route to generalist robots scales robotics data to train end-to-end policies. We instead use a vision-language model (VLM) as a coding agent that writes robot programs using a curated library of perception, planning, and control tools. MAESTRO’s orchestration harness packages multi-step perception and action procedures into callable tools and guides their use through a plan–act–replan loop, using visual and execution feedback to verify outcomes and recover from failures. With this tool library and harness, MAESTRO matches or surpasses state-of-the-art vision-language-action (VLA) models zero-shot in our tabletop comparison and performs diverse mobile manipulation tasks, without collecting new teleoperation data or invoking a VLA tool. Ablations show that expanding the tool library improves average task progress with the full harness, while adding tools without it does not reliably improve progress. Additional case studies examine cross-trial code improvement, VLA tool use, and autonomous seed demonstrations for downstream data augmentation. We argue that such agentic systems offer a complementary, far less-explored axis to data scaling for general-purpose robots. Project site: maestro-robot.github.io. Code: github.com/Beethoven-Q/maestro.
topics: 视觉语言动作与基础模型

papers.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human–Humanoid Interaction
papers.abstract: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. Our approach decomposes the problem into a high-level policy and a low-level policy. For the high-level policy, we introduce a shared-codebook VQ-VAE that tokenizes human and humanoid motion into a unified latent space, enabling cross-embodiment conditional generation via a Diffusion Forcing Transformer. The low-level policy uses a whole-body tracking controller for deployment on the Unitree G1. To train the system, we introduce a two-phase adaptive retargeting procedure that retargets one interaction partner to the robot while morphing the other partner to preserve contact dynamics, reachability, and relative body scale. We apply this procedure across five motion-capture datasets to produce a new Human-Humanoid Interaction (HHI) benchmark of 260 hours of paired human-humanoid interactions. Our results demonstrate that Social Humanoid produces coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interaction types in simulation and the real world.

papers.title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
papers.abstract: Current agentic robot systems can write executable Code-as-Policy programs, observe feedback, and revise behavior across multiple attempts, but they remain largely task-driven: reusable skills are acquired only after explicit instructions. We study Playful Agentic Robot Learning, where an embodied coding agent uses self-directed play as a continual skill-learning stage before downstream tasks arrive. We introduce RATs, a Robotics Agent Team designed for play-time skill acquisition. During play, RATs proposes novel yet learnable exploratory tasks, plans and executes robot-code policies, verifies intermediate progress, diagnoses failures, retries with feedback, and distills successful executions into a persistent code skill library. This structured agent team turns sparse task outcomes into dense feedback for learning reusable skills from autonomous interaction. Experiments in LIBERO-PRO and MolmoSpaces show that play-learned skills improve held-out downstream tasks over no play and random-play baselines, with a 20.6 and 17.0 percentage-point gains over CaP-Agent0 on LIBERO-PRO and MolmoSpaces, respectively. Moreover, the learned skills can be plugged into other inference-time Code-as-Policy agents by simply retrieving them into the context, improving RoboSuite transfer by 8.9 points without finetuning the model.

papers.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: The ability to react dynamically to tactile signals has long been considered crucial to agile human-level dexterity. Yet contemporary learning-based VLAs for robotic manipulation generally either overlook the tactile modality or are limited to encoders with static cues, in part due to  the scarcity of diverse training data and standardized evaluation, architectural constraints in current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and limitations of static tactile encoders. In this paper, we push the frontier of tactile-reactive manipulation addressing all of these limitations. We open-source a large-scale, 100-hour tactile-rich dataset collected via a novel, data-efficient recipe that prioritizes elementary motor primitives. To effectively exploit naturally high-frequency touch signals without sacrificing the existing capabilities of existing VLAs, we introduce a variable-rate Mix-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture equipped with a novel temporal tactile VQ-VAE encoder. We demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile-reactive policies on 12 manipulation tasks requiring delicate force control, deformable object manipulation, achieving over 30% higher average success rate than the strongest baseline.
